title: chore(linting): target correct folder
body:
closes #2443

<!--
  Thanks for submitting a pull request!
  Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request.
-->

**Summary**

sass-lint was being run on the generated docs instead of the source folder

**Result**

<!--
  Demonstrate the code is solid.
  Example: The exact commands you ran and their output,
  screenshots / videos if the pull request changes UI.
  
  You will be able to test out these changes on the deploy
  preview (address will be commented by a bot): 
  
  1. the documentation site (/)
  2. a widget playground (/dev-novel)
-->

* target correct folder
* ignore correct folders
* make hex rule a warning for now because we aren't consistent with it, we can fix it later when we want less warnings

comments.body:
Deploy preview ready!

Built with commit 6abf2dad9c3ca63554e499a228c3ac38d76f78e6

https://deploy-preview-2566--algolia-instantsearch.netlify.com
Will give it a try at fixing the sass lint problems :)
I did a pass on the rules and made the changes accordingly. I just have some questions about the rules around nesting and qualified elements. I'm pretty we should not enforce them. WDYT?
@bobylito Nice! IMO the nesting rule is pretty useless it's harder to read with the nested selector in some cases. For the other don't have a strong opinion on it..
@LukyVj @ronanlevesque maybe you can help us decide if we should ditch the last rules?

I would keep the `no-qualifying-elements` set to `false`. There are some edge cases when one might need to rely on them to enforce specific styles. Same for `nesting-depth`. It's hard to define an arbitrary depth for this as it can depends on a lot of things (eg nesting a modifier, then nesting a hover behaviour on the modifier etc.)

> I would keep the no-qualifying-elements set to false. There are some edge cases when one might need to rely on them to enforce specific styles. Same for nesting-depth.

Ok. What about I disable those rules for some files using `// sass-lint:disable`? @ronanlevesque 

The idea is that we are only using warning as it is the only to get all the errors at once. Of course then we should make sure that we never have warnings :)
It's updated @Haroenv @ronanlevesque if you want to have a look :)
